original_text: Reproductive Strategies Plants have a two-stage, alternating life cycle Sporophyteproduces haploid spores by meiosis Spores divide mitotically to become haploid gametophytes Gametophytes produce gametes Gametes fuse to produce a diploid zygote Zygote divides mitotically to become the diploid sporophyte
explanation: Plants undergo an alternation of generations, a life cycle that alternates between two multicellular stages: 1) The diploid (2n) sporophyte, which produces haploid (n) spores through meiosis. 2) These spores divide by mitosis to develop into the haploid (n) gametophyte. The gametophyte produces haploid gametes (sperm and egg) by mitosis. During fertilization, these gametes fuse to form a diploid (2n) zygote. The zygote then divides mitotically to grow into the diploid sporophyte, completing the cycle.

questions.q: In the plant alternation of generations life cycle, how are haploid spores produced?
opts: By fusion of male and female gametes
By active transport of pollen grains
questions.exp: The diploid sporophyte produces haploid spores through the process of meiosis.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of stages in alternation of generations starting from a haploid spore?
opts: Spore -> Mitosis -> Gametophyte -> Gametes -> Zygote -> Mitosis -> Sporophyte
Spore -> Meiosis -> Zygote -> Gametes -> Gametophyte -> Sporophyte
Spore -> Gamete -> Zygote -> Meiosis -> Sporophyte -> Gametophyte
questions.exp: A haploid spore divides by mitosis to form a gametophyte. The gametophyte produces gametes, which fuse to form a zygote. The zygote divides by mitosis to form the sporophyte.
